# Results — Study 714 ("Contemporary art is an asset class")

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Does contemporary art beat the
S&P? We test the strongest tradable version of the art-as-investment claim: a secondary-
market **auction price index** (hardcoded, cited, **approximate** — a labelled proxy, not a
live feed) and the only **listed** ways to touch the trade (MCH Group `MCHN.SW`, organiser of
Art Basel; Kering `KER.PA`, whose owner Pinault controls Christie's), each benchmarked
against `SPY`. Offline & deterministic; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every
number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Art index | **Hardcoded, cited, approximate** annual secondary-market auction level (base 100 @ 2000-12-31), reconstructed from public Artprice / Sotheby's Mei Moses / press reporting — see [`docs/references.md`](references.md). **A PROXY, not a feed.** |
| Equity proxies | `MCHN.SW` (MCH Group / Art Basel, SIX) · `KER.PA` (Kering / Christie's-via-Pinault, Euronext) — month-end Adj Close via yfinance, cached under `_cache/` |
| Benchmark | `SPY` (month-end Adj Close, yfinance) |
| As-of | 2025-12-31 (month-end; no partial-year bar) |
| Equity window | 2000-01 → 2025-12 (KER/SPY: 312 months; MCHN.SW from its 2001 listing: 295 months) |
| Delisted / private (no listed way to buy) | **Sotheby's `BID`** — taken private by Patrick Drahi, June 2019 · **Christie's** — private (Artémis/Pinault) · **Phillips** — private (Mercury) |

> **Why proxies, stated as a decision.** Real art indices (Artprice's Global / Contemporary
> Art Market report, the Sotheby's Mei Moses repeat-sales index) are **not freely
> API-available**. Rather than fabricate a live tape we (a) hardcode a small, clearly-cited,
> **approximate** annual series whose *shape* — a 2000s melt-up, a 2008–09 crash, a 2014 peak,
> the 2021–22 records boom and the 2023–24 correction — is the load-bearing public fact, and
> (b) test the **listed** proxies a public investor can actually buy. Uniquely here the
> cleanest expressions (the auction houses themselves) are all **private**, so the equity set
> is a stated second-best; a fair organiser's and a luxury group's equity are **not** the
> hammer price of a painting.

## Half 1 — did the art beat the S&P? (art index vs SPY)

The (approximate, cited) secondary-market auction index, year-end levels base 100:

| year | 2000 | 2003 | 2007 | 2009 | 2014 | 2019 | 2021 | 2022 | 2024 | 2025 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| level | 100 | 108 | **268** | 150 | 330 | 345 | 430 | **478** | 385 | 400 |

The market ran twice and gave it back twice: from the **2007 pre-crisis peak** it crashed
**−44.0%** into the 2009 trough; from the **2022 records peak** (spring-2022 ≈ level 490 on
this scale; the Macklowe collection alone made **$922M**) it corrected **−19.5%** into 2024.
Headline risk/return vs SPY:

| series | CAGR | ann. vol | Sharpe | max drawdown |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Art auction index** | **+5.70%** | 17.1% | 0.41 | **−44.0%** |
| SPY (year-end) | **+8.76%** | 17.8% | — | −36.8% |

**The art lost the race:** ~5.7%/yr vs ~8.8%/yr for the S&P, with a *deeper* drawdown on the
same annual clock. The mean annual excess (index − SPY) is **−3.27%/yr**, **t = −0.69**
(p = 0.50, n = 25 years) — i.e. it underperformed, comfortably inside noise: "no evidence art
beats stocks, and the point estimate is negative."

## Half 2 — the tradable proxies vs SPY (the only thing you can buy)

Monthly Adj Close, Newey-West (6-lag) alpha vs SPY. **These are labelled proxies** — and note
the pure auction houses (Sotheby's, Christie's, Phillips) are all private, so there is no
clean listed expression at all.

| series | CAGR | ann. vol | Sharpe | max DD | alpha/yr | beta | NW *t*(α) | p |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **MCHN.SW** (Art Basel) | **−6.85%** | 31.5% | −0.07 | **−95.5%** | −7.74% | 0.60 | −1.11 | 0.27 |
| **KER.PA** (Kering) | +4.84% | 32.6% | 0.31 | −78.9% | −0.15% | 1.12 | −0.03 | 0.98 |
| SPY | +8.23% | 15.1% | **0.60** | −50.8% | — | — | — | — |

Neither proxy shows a *significant* alpha vs SPY (|t| ≪ 2). **MCH Group — the one directly
art-market-linked listed equity — lost money outright and fell −95.5%** peak-to-trough: the
art-fair business is a disastrous proxy for art prices going up. Kering underperformed SPY at
twice the volatility with no alpha. **No harvestable alpha in either.**

## Half 3 — the buyer's-premium / carry haircut (what a round-trip really costs)

The pitch never charges the friction. A published index tracks **hammer** prices; a real
collector buys at hammer **+ ~25% buyer's premium** and sells receiving hammer **− ~10%
seller's commission** — a round-trip multiple of `0.90 / 1.25 = 0.720` (a ~28% haircut),
amortised over a ~**7-year** hold, plus ~**1%/yr** insurance/storage. Charged once on the
index's gross CAGR:

| | value |
|---|--:|
| gross CAGR (index) | +5.70%/yr |
| − buyer+seller premium drag (0.72 over 7y) | −4.58%/yr |
| − insurance/storage carry | −1.00%/yr |
| **= NET CAGR a real collector earns** | **−0.15%/yr** |

The 5.7% gross *that already lost to the S&P* turns **negative** once you pay to actually
transact and hold the work. T-bills beat it; the S&P laps it.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is faithful

A deterministic, fixed-seed "bubble-and-round-trip" path (planted boom CAGR +35%, bust −22%,
σ = 4.5%/mo, seed 714): the inference engine recovers the planted up-sign and a finite Sharpe
— peak ≈ 589 → end ≈ 175, recovered CAGR **+5.31%**, Sharpe 0.39, max DD −70.3%,
`sign_ok = 1`. The harness can bank a planted signal, so a null on the real proxies is a real
null, not a broken pipeline.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE (it *under*-performs).** Over 2000–2025 the art index returned ~5.7%/yr vs
  ~8.8%/yr for SPY; the annual excess is **−3.27%/yr (t = −0.69)** — no evidence art beats
  stocks, and the point estimate is negative. The proxies show **no significant alpha**
  (|t| ≪ 2). The "contemporary art is an asset class that beats the S&P" claim fails on the
  tape it's quoted on.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Even the gross index CAGR (5.7%) goes **negative (−0.15%/yr)**
  after a realistic ~25% buyer's premium + carry; the auction houses are all private (no
  listed way to buy them), and the buyable proxies are worse — MCH Group (Art Basel) *lost*
  money and drew down −95.5%. Illiquid, high-premium, two round-trips.
- **"Art beats the S&P?" — BUSTED.** On return, risk-adjusted return, drawdown *and*
  net-of-cost, the S&P wins every column. The few who "made money" bought a specific name
  early and sold it at a record — survivors of a boom, not an asset class.

> **Caveat (named, not buried).** The art index here is a **small, hardcoded, approximate**
> reconstruction of public reporting — its *level path/shape* is defensible but its precise
> year-end values are not a live feed, and the annual *t* rests on 25 observations of a
> smoothed series. The equity proxies are exactly that — proxies for "owning the art trade,"
> not the hammer price of a painting. Both limitations push the verdict toward humility, not
> toward a stronger claim: nothing here says art beats stocks, and several lines say the
> opposite.
